units.text: INT. WOMAN - CONTINUOUS
You must remember, as you said yourself, you have had so few advantages.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Lord Illingworth, I want to speak to you for a moment. Do come over.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Will you excuse me, Mrs. Arbuthnot? Now, don’t let your charming mother make any more difficulties, Gerald. The thing is quite settled, isn’t it?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: I hope so.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: LORD ILLINGWORTH goes across to MRS. ARBUTHNOT.
I thought you were never going to leave the lady in black velvet.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: She is excessively handsome.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Looks at MRS. ARBUTHNOT.
Caroline, shall we all make a move to the music-room? Miss Worsley is going to play. You’ll come too, dear Mrs. Arbuthnot, won’t you? You don’t know what a treat is in store for you.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: To Doctor Daubeny.

I must really take Miss Worsley down some afternoon to the rectory. I should so much like dear Mrs. Daubeny to hear her on the violin. Ah, I forgot. Dear Mrs. Daubeny’s hearing is a little defective, is it not?
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: Her deafness is a great privation to her. She can’t even hear my sermons now. She reads them at home. But she has many resources in herself, many resources.
units.name: THE ARCHDEACON

units.text: She reads a good deal, I suppose?
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: Just the very largest print. The eyesight is rapidly going. But she’s never morbid, never morbid.
units.name: THE ARCHDEACON

units.text: To LORD ILLINGWORTH.
Do speak to my mother, Lord Illingworth, before you go into the music-room. She seems to think, somehow, you don’t mean what you said to me.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Aren’t you coming?
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: In a few moments. Lady Hunstanton, if Mrs. Arbuthnot would allow me, I would like to say a few words to her, and we will join you later on.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Ah, of course. You will have a great deal to say to her, and she will have a great deal to thank you for. It is not every son who gets such an offer, Mrs. Arbuthnot. But I know you appreciate that, dear.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: John!
units.name: LADY CAROLINE

units.text: Now, don’t keep Mrs. Arbuthnot too long, Lord Illingworth. We can’t spare her.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: Exit following the other guests .
Sound of violin heard from music-room .
So that is our son, Rachel! Well, I am very proud of him. He is a Harford, every inch of him. By the way, why Arbuthnot, Rachel?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: One name is as good as another, when one has no right to any name.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: I suppose so—but why Gerald?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: After a man whose heart I broke—after my father.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Well, Rachel, what is over is over. All I have got to say now in that I am very, very much pleased with our boy. The world will know him merely as my private secretary, but to me he will be something very near, and very dear. It is a curious thing, Rachel; my life seemed to be quite complete. It was not so. It lacked something, it lacked a son. I have found my son now, I am glad I have found him.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: You have no right to claim him, or the smallest part of him. The boy is entirely mine, and shall remain mine.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: My dear Rachel, you have had him to yourself for over twenty years. Why not let me have him for a little now? He is quite as much mine as yours.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Are you talking of the child you abandoned? Of the child who, as far as you are concerned, might have died of hunger and of want?
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: You forget, Rachel, it was you who left me. It was not I who left you.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: I left you because you refused to give the child a name. Before my son was born, I implored you to marry me.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: I had no expectations then. And besides, Rachel, I wasn’t much older than you were. I was only twenty-two. I was twenty-one, I believe, when the whole thing began in your father’s garden.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: When a man is old enough to do wrong he should be old enough to do right also.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: My dear Rachel, intellectual generalities are always interesting, but generalities in morals mean absolutely nothing. As for saying I left our child to starve, that, of course, is untrue and silly. My mother offered you six hundred a year. But you wouldn’t take anything. You simply disappeared, and carried the child away with you.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: I wouldn’t have accepted a penny from her. Your father was different. He told you, in my presence, when we were in Paris, that it was your duty to marry me.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Oh, duty is what one expects from others, it is not what one does oneself. Of course, I was influenced by my mother. Every man is when he is young.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: I am glad to hear you say so. Gerald shall certainly not go away with you.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: What nonsense, Rachel!
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Do you think I would allow my son—
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Our son.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: My son
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: LORD ILLINGWORTH shrugs his shoulders.
—to go away with the man who spoiled my youth, who ruined my life, who has tainted every moment of my days? You don’t realise what my past has been in suffering and in shame.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: My dear Rachel, I must candidly say that I think Gerald’s future considerably more important than your past.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH
